articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: The best reliable, under-the-radar QB options for Week 3
articles.description: With injury questions surrounding several QBs in the league, let's take a look at some underrated QBs.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 23: Need a QB before Week 3? The best reliable, under-the-radar options

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

You couldn't find much more contrast between Weeks 1 and 2 of this NFL season.

A week after the NFL matched the opening-week record for points scored (791), the 32 teams combined to score only 647 in Week 2. Per ESPN Research, the 647 are the fewest points in any non-Week 18 slate since Week 2 of the 2024 season.

Injuries had quite a bit to do with it, particularly at the quarterback position. Through two weeks, we've already seen five starters depart games due to injury, and that excludes the Atlanta Falcons' two combatants for their starting job (Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr.) who have yet to play in 2026. Among the quarterbacks expected to be absent for Week 3 are three members of the position's top 10 in terms of ADP (average draft position): Jayden Daniels, Jaxson Dart and Caleb Williams.

These high-profile injury setbacks have sent many a fantasy manager scrambling to find a quality quarterback, and there are plenty of options out there to be had -- standard, Knockout, Vampire, etc., leagues alike. Three in particular stand out, players who went 17th or later at the position in the preseason but are suddenly viable starters:

Tyler Shough, New Orleans Saints: His Consistency Ratings won't reflect it due to his initial backup status to begin last season, but if we splice Shough's results into the games he started versus served in a backup capacity, he has been remarkably reliable. He's one of five quarterbacks to score 20-plus fantasy points in each of 2026's first two weeks, finishing eighth in scoring at the position in each, and he has been a top-10 scorer in five of his past seven starts.

Shough still has inconsistencies, especially with how deliberate he has been with his throws early in those games (not to mention taking too many sacks), but the mettle he has shown while leading his team to an overtime loss and a win over the Baltimore Ravens speaks highly for his future potential. Shough is already in my top 10 rankings for Week 3 (LV) -- he was my must-get in our staff Vampire league -- and he has a good matchup for Week 4 (ATL), too.

Shough, incidentally, leads all quarterbacks in expected fantasy points, yet he's still out there in 32.1% of ESPN leagues.

articles.descriptionJa: NBAトップ100選手のカウントダウンは続きます。トップ10入りを惜しくも逃したスター選手たちや、3人のレジェンドが何位にランクインしたかをご覧ください。
articles.body:
NBA Rank is back! With less than one month until opening night, let's continue counting down the league's best players for 2026-27.

After unveiling players Nos. 100-51 on Tuesday, our rankings now enter the top 50. It's a group headlined by former MVPs, future first-ballot Hall of Famers and young stars expected to take major leaps this season.  

It's also where LeBron James checks in, his first time outside the top 10 in NBA Rank's 15-year history. (You can jump to LeBron's NBA Rank here.)

The rankings rollout concludes Thursday with our expert panel's top 10 players. And that panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition.

In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list. That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list, which features plenty of superstars who just missed our top 10.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

50. Dylan Harper

G | San Antonio Spurs

Age: 20

2025 NBA Rank: NR

The youngest member of the Spurs was the one who seemed to rise highest in the altitude of the Finals and stands to make a big jump in Year 2, whether he stays coming off the bench or makes the leap to the first five. He will earn more respect from the officials (1.7 free throw attempts in 69 games as a rookie), take a bigger role in the offense and improve on his already-respectable playmaking. Harper is an All-Star in the making. -- Vincent Goodwill

Signature stat: Harper had six games with at least 15 points and 65% shooting from the field in the 2026 playoffs, the most by a guard in NBA postseason history.

Fantasy projection: 15.2 PTS, 5.0 AST, 4.4 REB

49. Lauri Markkanen

F | Utah Jazz

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 43

Markkanen, a scoring forward who can stretch the court, has languished as a forgotten man in Utah. The Finnish star's competence often came into conflict with the Jazz's desire to improve their draft positioning during a multiyear rebuilding effort, and he has appeared in only one game in April over the past four seasons. Though his contract is overly generous for a player lacking All-NBA credentials, Markkanen should benefit from Utah's recent talent upgrades as he eyes his first career postseason appearance. -- Ben Golliver

Signature stat: Markkanen has nine seasons with at least 100 3-pointers, tied with Karl-Anthony Towns and Dirk Nowitzki for the most by a 7-footer in NBA history.

Fantasy projection: 23.8 PTS, 7.2 REB, 1.9 AST

48. Kon Knueppel

G | Charlotte

Sept. 23: Wednesday's news to know

By Todd Zola

Today's action gets underway at 1:10 p.m. ET with an interleague affair in Motown. The Detroit Tigers host the Washington Nationals in a game between clubs playing out the string.

For the second straight day, a pair of teams will be taking the field twice, with the Toronto Blue Jays and Baltimore Orioles making up yesterday's rainout with a separate-admission doubleheader at Camden Yards. The good news is that Mother Nature should cooperate today, with early forecasts favorable everywhere. The bad news is that things could get ugly this weekend, with rain expected in the Northeast.

The Los Angeles Dodgers expect to have Shohei Ohtani serving as their designated hitter when they host the San Diego Padres this evening. Manager Dave Roberts indicated that Ohtani will be examined today, and barring a surprise, he'll return to the lineup. He's been convalescing on the 10-day IL, taking care of lingering knee and biceps issues.

Ceddanne Rafaela is expected to return to the Boston Red Sox lineup tonight when they host the Cleveland Guardians. The Gold Glove center fielder has been out for over two weeks with a right quad strain. Nate Eaton will return to his reserve role.

Ronald Acuna Jr. had to leave last night's Atlanta Braves game in the third inning after fouling a ball off his left shin. He was able to walk off the field with no assistance, and X-rays were negative, so the club is hopeful that he won't miss much time, if any. Brewer Hicklen finished Acuna's at-bat last night and would be the likely replacement if needed.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Wednesday. 

Sept. 22: Tuesday's news to know

By Todd Zola

articles.headline: NFL Week 3 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips
articles.description: What now for the Giants with Jaxson Dart out? What's the buzz on Patrick Mahomes through two games? Are running back depth charts firming up in Tampa and Carolina?
articles.body:
We're onto Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season, and insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been making calls to sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

There was optimism around the Giants coming into Week 2, but things went south quickly Monday night. They lost their quarterback on the first drive and lost the game in a 28-6 blowout. How are the vibes in their building and where do they go with Jaxson Dart out? On the other end of the spectrum, the Chiefs moved to 2-0 with Patrick Mahomes back from last season's torn ACL. What are people saying about his play?

Around the league, we have a sample size to draw some conclusions. What looks different through two weeks from our preseason expectations? And which previously uncertain running back hierarchies are getting clarity? It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 3.

Jump to:

Next steps for the Giants

Early thoughts on Mahomes

Preseason take do-overs

Updates on RB depth charts

Fantasy football advice

More notes and intel

What are you hearing out of the Giants' building?

Graziano: They're disappointed, obviously. They had designed a game plan for their Monday night game against the Rams around Jaxson Dart, believing his mobility would help mitigate the interior pressure they knew they were going to face from Aaron Donald and the L.A. defensive front, and they suddenly had to play a far less mobile Jameis Winston. The run game was limited once the Rams didn't have to worry about the quarterback run threat. They thought they could get more pressure on Matthew Stafford than they did. Very disappointing night all around.

They do believe Winston will be better with a full week of practice as the starter and with a game plan built around his strengths. We are waiting to find out whether they will have Malik Nabers, Andrew Thomas or Brian Burns, all of whom also left Monday night's game due to injuries. That becomes much more important because the Dart injury has turned out to be more serious than they believed Monday night.

Fowler: Your point about the game plan is an important one -- the Giants entered Monday's game with a plan tailored around Dart's skill set. But now the Giants' offense is in the hands of Winston, who signed a two-year, $13 million extension on Sept. 6. Winston is comfortable operating out of the shotgun, which offensive coordinator Matt Nagy -- with his ties to Kansas City and Andy Reid -- can accommodate.

But man, the Giants offense looked so good in Week 1 with Dart under center, operating at a high level and making quick decisions (Dallas' defense contributed to that, to be sure). And then it looked so sloppy without him, especially in that end-of-half sequence in the red zone Monday night. This is where Nabers enters the fray. articles.headline: Man United transfer strategy 'financial sustainable' as losses increase - CEO
articles.description: Manchester United's summer transfer strategy had "financial sustainability in mind," according to CEO Omar Berrada, after reporting a increased financial losses.
articles.headlineJa: 赤字拡大もマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの移籍戦略は「財政的に持続可能」とCEOが主張
articles.descriptionJa: 赤字の拡大が報告されたのを受け、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのオマル・ベラダCEOは、今夏の移籍戦略は「財政的な持続可能性を念頭に置いたもの」だったと述べた。
articles.body:
Manchester United's summer transfer strategy had "financial sustainability in mind," according to CEO Omar Berrada, after the club reported increased financial losses.

On Wednesday, United posted record full year revenues of £677.6m ($900m) and an operating profit of £22.6m ($30m).

However, the club still reported an overall loss of £43m ($57m), up from £33m ($44m) the previous year.

Borrowing increased by £95m ($126m) to a total of £583m ($773m).

United spent £155m ($206m) midfielders Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba in the transfer window.

Big six rivals Manchester City, Liverpool, Arsenal, Tottenham and Chelsea all spent considerably more with City, Liverpool, Tottenham and Chelsea all spending at least £100m ($133) on one player.

And speaking as the club's fourth quarter and full year financial results were published on Wednesday, Berrada hinted at a need for a prudent approach to transfers.

"While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable," Berrada said.

"With that financial sustainability in mind, we have strengthened both our men's and women's teams during the summer window and our men's team has seen the return of Champions League football to Old Trafford."

- Carrick quashes notion Manchester United are out of shape

- Mikel Arteta agrees a new long-term contract extension with Arsenal - sources

In the news release which accompanied the results, United said: "the club continues on its journey to improve operational efficiency and financial sustainability."

A United source said "stabilising the business has required, and will continue to require, hard work and financial discipline."

Among the expenditures for the year was £8.2m ($11m) paid to Ruben Amorim and his staff after the Portuguese coach was dismissed in January. United saved around £8.5m ($11.3m) after Amorim accepted the head coach job at AC Milan in the summer.

The club also paid off around £150m ($199m) from a revolving credit facility between March and June.

Meanwhile, United's finances revealed they paid £63.5m ($84m) for land associated with plans to build a new stadium.

Berrada said: "Our other main area of focus is our plan to develop a new 100,000 seater stadium. We have now completed the major milestone of securing the land which will form part of the proposed location of the new stadium."

articles.headline: Full final 2026 regular-season grades for all 30 MLB teams
articles.description: Whether your team is headed to October or packing its bags for the offseason, how did 2026 measure up to expectations?
articles.headlineJa: MLB全30球団の2026年レギュラーシーズン最終採点
articles.descriptionJa: 応援するチームが10月のポストシーズンに向かうのか、それともオフシーズンを迎えるのかにかかわらず、2026年シーズンは期待通りの結果となったでしょうか？
articles.body:
As we wrap up the 2026 Major League Baseball regular season, it's time for some final grades.

As expected, the Los Angeles Dodgers challenged the single-season record for wins. The New York Mets had a huge offseason that paid off with the National League East title. The New York Yankees dominated the American League East. The Milwaukee Brewers failed to scrap their way to the playoffs. Tarik Skubal carried the Detroit Tigers to the AL Central championship. The Chicago White Sox? A joke once again.

Wait ... no, that's not at all what happened. The only joke -- outside of the usual ineptitude we see from the clubs at the bottom of the majors -- was the AL West, which might see a team with a losing record capture the division title.

The 2026 season might not have gone as expected, but we still had breakout performances, surprising teams, unpredictable results, a flamethrowing phenom, a season for the ages and a very mediocre AL. Let's go to the grades.

Milwaukee Brewers: A+

What a wonderful, engaging and thrilling regular season for the Brewers. They've already set the franchise record for wins in a single season, breaking last year's mark of 97, and are heading to the top record in the majors for the second year in a row. Jacob Misiorowski has been the best individual story of the season -- alongside division rival Pete Crow-Armstrong -- but it has been an impressive teamwide effort.

Milwaukee's rookie pitchers have started 77 games, most in the majors, while another pair of rookies in shortstop Cooper Pratt and right fielder Luis Lara will be starting in October. Brice Turang's 6.9 bWAR is second among MLB position players, and he should finish in the top five of the MVP voting. Oh, and the bullpen is top five in the majors in win probability added.

Not bad for a team that was 11th in ESPN's preseason power rankings. At least we got "the thing we'll be talking about most this season" right for Milwaukee: Misiorowski's sophomore year.

Tampa Bay Rays: A+

Nope, the Rays never faded. In fact, they went 18-10 in August and are 14-6 in September after clinching the division (and the top record in the AL) with a win over the Yankees on Tuesday.

Tampa Bay has been a little hard to analyze at times as it has gone 25-14 in one-run games, which helps erase its 22-23 record in blowout games decided by five-plus. (Good teams almost always have a winning record in blowout games, so this is a weird anomaly.) While Junior Caminero has been a standout and Jonathan Aranda is closing in on 100 RBIs, it has been a year of unsung heroes: Nick Martinez and Drew Rasmussen lead the rotation with 15 wins apiece and sub 3.00 ERAs; Griffin Jax transitioned from reliever to starter; Bryan Baker leads the majors in saves; Victor Mesa Jr. added surprising power in the second half.

You can ask the same question about the Brewers and the Rays: Will this be the year?

Atlanta Braves: A

articles.headline: Sources: Mikel Arteta agrees a new long-term contract extension with Arsenal
articles.description: Arsenal are expected to announce Mikel Arteta has signed a new long-term contract after the 44-year-old agreed terms to stay on as manager, sources have told ESPN.
articles.body:
Arsenal are expected to announce Mikel Arteta has signed a new long-term contract after the team and the 44-year-old manager agreed on terms, sources have told ESPN.

Arteta's current deal expires at the end of the season, but the Spaniard has repeatedly stated his intention to remain at the club he joined in December 2019.

Sources say all parties have been relaxed about the situation for several months with an agreement likely to be finalized during a pause in the domestic campaign.

Arsenal do not play again until Oct. 10 as a result of the newly extended international break and confirmation that Arteta has signed a new contract could come before then.

The Gunners declined to comment when contacted by ESPN but Arteta is set for a significant pay rise on his current salary which sources say can reach £15 million ($20M) with bonuses.

- Sunderland penalty against Arsenal incorrect - Premier League panel

- Mourinho's ref rants overshadow Madrid derby defeat; can Arsenal shrug off heavy loss?

"I'm extremely happy and I feel very grateful to work with the people I work with," said Arteta when asked about his contract situation last week.

Arteta ended Arsenal's 22-year wait for a Premier League title in May and last month, he registered his 150th league win from 249 games -- only Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Sir Alex Ferguson have achieved the milestone quicker.
